data.body:
═══ CORRECTION TO TWO CLAIMS I MADE ON THIS TICKET, and a landing blocker discovered downstream ═══

An independent landing-safety assessment of the epic stack checked my blast-radius analysis against
this repo's ACTUAL config and found two of my claims wrong. Correcting them here because the wrong
version is recorded above and a later reader would inherit it.

**WRONG CLAIM 1: "plan-review's runner floor is `cfg.model`."** It is not.
`plan_review/__init__.py:609` calls `produce_plan_review_verdict(ctx, _verifier_cfg(cfg), …)`, so the
ENTIRE plan-review run's `runner._config.model` is already `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`, not the
`claude-opus-4-8` default. I reasoned as though plan-review shared code-review's floor. It does not.

**WRONG CLAIM 2: "this fix makes four previously-inert per-call configs effective."** Only ONE of the
four. Because the floor is ALREADY `_verifier_cfg(cfg)` and `_verifier_cfg` is IDEMPOTENT
(`_verifier_cfg(floor).model == floor.model` → True), and because `_effective_config` returns `base`
unchanged when `requested == base.model`, the three `_verifier_cfg` sub-call sites
(`xcheck.py:199`, `xcheck.py:337`, `plan_review/__init__.py:164`) are **NO-OPS under this config** —
nothing moves. Only `prerequisites.py:226`'s `call_cfg` becomes live. So my "three Pass-2 sub-calls
move frontier → verifier model" statement was wrong in both direction and count: they were already on
sonnet.

**AND THE CONSEQUENCE I MISSED ENTIRELY — filed as bug `77ed`, and it is a LANDING BLOCKER.** Because
plan-review's floor is sonnet while Pass-1's `model_ladder[0]` is `trivial`, this fix moves the
plan-review **Pass-1 FINDER** from sonnet to **haiku**. That is the pass that GENERATES the findings
which become blocking and gate every `claim`. `origin/main`'s own `_verifier_cfg` docstring claims
"The Pass-1 finder is unaffected: it runs the YAML `model_ladder` via the ProductionBatchRunner, not
`cfg.model`" — that comment is FALSE on main, and this change is what makes it true. Pass-1 has
declared the cheapest rung since the workflow was created and has never once run on it.

Nothing about this ticket's own work is wrong: it made declarations effective, which is what it set
out to do. One of those declarations turns out to be undesirable, and the ladder does not compensate
because it escalates on CONTEXT LIMIT, not on quality. Full evidence, the measured pre/post models,
and the one-line mitigation (raise the Pass-1 entry rung from `trivial` to `standard`) are on `77ed`.

**Why neither CI nor this ticket's tests could catch it:** the offline suite substitutes
`FunctionModel`/`FakeRunner` for precisely the thing that changes — which model a live gate calls. The
stack tip is green on lint, typecheck and the full unit suite, and that greenness carries no
information about this class of risk. Worth remembering the next time "CI is green" is offered as
evidence that a model-routing change is safe.
